The facts in brief of the revision are that the revisionist/ complainant, which is a society, gave a loan of Rs.50,00,000/- to the respondent no. 1, of which respondent no. 2 is the proprietor. Respondents submitted post dated cheques bearing no. 970268 for an amount of Rs. 13,15,445/- to the revisionist which got dishonored on presentation and thereafter notice was served upon the Small Farmers Agri Business Consortium vs M/S Maya Aromatics Proprietorship And ... on 27 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96280825/ 1 respondents. However, despite service of notice the respondents did not pay the cheque amount. Hence, a complaint was filed by the revisionist against respondents for offense under Section 138 NI Act. Vide order dated 29.11.2021, Ld. Trial Court found sufficient grounds to proceed against the respondents u/s 138 NI Act and accordingly, issued summons against them, to which respondents entered their appearance on 07.07.2022. 3. Thereafter, matter was listed on several dates and on 30.05.2023, the complaint was compounded and the accused were discharged. 4. Being aggrieved, the revisionist has filed the present petition on the ground that the impugned order of Ld. MM passed on 30.05.2023 is totally illegal and contrary to law because: - i. Ld. Following observations made by Ld. Magistrate in his impugned order, are relevant: "Counsel for the complainant submits that the total amount qua cheque in question has been received.
texts.arguments: 7. Ld. counsel for the revisionist argued that the impugned order has been passed without the consent of the complainant, hence, the same is liable to be set-aside and the complaint may be restored to its original number. On the other hand, Ld. counsel for the respondents has argued that against an order of acquittal, the complainant can only file an application u/s 378 (4) Cr.P.C. for special leave to appeal in the High Court and not a revision against it in Sessions Court. In support of his contention he relied upon judgments passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case titled as Betcon Dickinson India Ltd Vs. Shika Pharma (P) Ltd. & Anr and in case titled as Pratima Goel and Anr. Vs. Metropolitan Magistrate & Anr. 9. Ld. counsel for the respondents has contended that the revision under Section 397/399 of Cr.P.C. is not maintainable against the impugned order. 12. Compounding of offence is provided u/s 147 of NI Act which reads as under :- "Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), every offence punishable under this Act shall be compoundable." 13. At this stage, it would be relevant to quote provisions of Section 378(4) Cr.P.C. which are as under: 378. Appeal in case of acquittal (1)......... (2)......... (3)......... (4) If such an order of acquittal is passed in any case instituted upon complaint and the High Court, on an application made to it by the complainant in this behalf, grants special leave to appeal from the order of acquittal, the complainant may present such an appeal to the High Court" . PURSHOTTAM PURSHOTTAM PATHAK 2024.01.27 16:25:12 +0530 laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subhash Chand Vs State (Delhi Administration), 2013 (1) JCC 338, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court in para nos. 17 and 21 held as under:- "17. It was a complaint case under Section 7 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, in which Subhash Chand was tried and he was acquitted by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate.
